title: Audit Log Event Taxonomy — Optimization Config (Safe apply + rollback) [working sheet]
content:
Context / why this exists
- Feature: Safe apply + rollback mechanism for Optimization Configs (batching, caching, quantization profiles).
- Enterprise ask: complete, queryable, exportable audit trail of all config lifecycle actions with strong actor attribution + before/after context.
- This sheet is the proposed event taxonomy + required fields. It’s intended to unblock:
  - product/security review (Naomi / Marcus)
  - engineering implementation (ENG-4826)
  - SIEM export mapping (Splunk/Datadog/Chronicle)

Non-goals (for v1)
- Not designing the entire audit pipeline; focusing on event names + payload schema.
- Not defining every metric/tag used for rollout gating; only what needs to appear in audit.

Principles
1) Every operator action that can change runtime behavior must generate an audit event.
2) Events must be: immutable, append-only, time-ordered (within reasonable clock skew bounds), and exportable.
3) Include enough fields to answer: who did what, to what scope, when, from where, what changed, what was the result, and how to correlate across systems.
4) Avoid leaking sensitive content (no prompts, no raw config blobs if they contain secrets/keys).

Terminology (aligning across teams)
- Optimization Config: top-level object (per tenant/model/region scope) controlling batching/caching/quant settings.
- Version: immutable snapshot; version_id is stable. “Active version” is a pointer per scope.
- Rollout: staged apply (canary %, shard-based, etc.) resulting in active version change over time.
- Scope: tuple of tenant_id + (model_id | model_family) + region + deployment_mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

Event naming conventions (proposal)
- Namespace: "optimization_config".
- Format: optimization_config.<noun>.<verb>
  - Example: optimization_config.version.created
- All events include: event_name, occurred_at, outcome, and stable correlation identifiers.

Event taxonomy (v1)

A) Version lifecycle
1. optimization_config.version.created
   - When a new immutable version is created.
   - Trigger: API/Console/automation.

2. optimization_config.version.validation_requested
   - Operator requested validation (schema + semantic). Separate from apply.

3. optimization_config.version.validation_succeeded
4. optimization_config.version.validation_failed
   - Include failure_class + validation_errors summary.

5. optimization_config.version.deleted (NOTE: do we allow this?)
   - Strong default: NO deletion; only “retracted” or “superseded”.
   - If deletion exists for non-prod/test tenants, must be logged.

B) Rollout / apply workflow
6. optimization_config.rollout.started
   - A rollout job created to move a given scope from current active version to target version.

7. optimization_config.rollout.progressed
   - Rollout moved to next stage (e.g., 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
   - We may throttle emission (stage boundaries only) to avoid noisy logs.

8. optimization_config.rollout.paused
9. optimization_config.rollout.resumed
10. optimization_config.rollout.canceled
   - Canceled != rollback. Rollout may stop mid-way; active version could be mixed by shard until repaired.

11. optimization_config.rollout.completed
   - Completed successfully; active pointer set for scope.

12. optimization_config.rollout.failed
   - Include failure_reason + failed_stage + whether automatic rollback was executed.

C) Promotion semantics (if we support environments)
13. optimization_config.version.promoted
   - Promotion from "staging" -> "prod" OR from "candidate" -> "blessed".
   - Needs explicit source_env, target_env.

D) Rollback workflow
14. optimization_config.rollback.requested
   - User initiated rollback action (Console button/API call).

15. optimization_config.rollback.completed
16. optimization_config.rollback.failed
   - Must include from_version_id, to_version_id, rollback_scope.

E) Access control / authorization relevant to audit
17. optimization_config.authorization.denied
   - When a principal attempts an apply/rollback action without permissions.
   - Useful for incident investigations and customer security review.

F) Integrations / external signals (optional for v1, but requested by SRE)
18. optimization_config.gate.evaluation_started
19. optimization_config.gate.evaluation_failed
20. optimization_config.gate.evaluation_succeeded
   - NOTE: These are *not* human actions, but have compliance value (prove gates existed).
   - If we decide to log them, keep payload minimal and avoid metric spam.

Payload schema: required fields (applies to all events)

Core envelope
- event_name: string (see taxonomy)
- event_version: string (e.g., "1") — allows schema changes without breaking exports
- occurred_at: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC)
- emitted_at: RFC3339 timestamp (UTC) (when written to audit store) — helps identify pipeline delays
- environment: string (prod | staging | dev | private) — private = customer control plane
- outcome: string (success | failure | denied | partial)
- severity: string (info | warning | critical)

Actor attribution
- actor_type: string (user | service | system)
- actor_id: string (redwood_user_id OR service principal id)
- actor_email: string (if user and available; ok to omit for service)
- actor_role: string (RBAC role at time of action; important even if role later changes)
- authn_method: string (sso | api_key | oauth | session)
- authz_policy: string (policy bundle version/hash used for decision)

Request context
- request_id: string (edge request id)
- trace_id: string (distributed trace id) (optional but strongly recommended)
- console_session_id: string (if initiated via Console)
- source: string (console | public_api | internal_api | automation | private_operator)
- client_ip: string (or best-effort; for private deployments may be "customer_network")
- user_agent: string (if available)

Target identifiers
- tenant_id: string
- org_id: string (if tenant maps to org; optional but requested by enterprise)
- deployment_mode: string (hosted | dedicated | private)
- region: string (e.g., us-east-1)
- model_id: string (e.g., "rw-llama-3-70b") or "*" for wildcard scope

Config identifiers
- optimization_config_id: string (stable id for config object)
- target_version_id: string (immutable)
- previous_version_id: string (if applicable)
- rollout_id: string (for rollout events)
- change_id: string (stable id that ties create/validate/apply/rollback events for one "change")

Human intent / justification (required for apply + rollback)
- reason: string (free text; enforced non-empty for production scopes)
- ticket_ref: string (Jira/Linear/Incident id; enforced for prod)
- approver_id: string (optional for v1; likely required by some customers)
- approver_email: string (optional)

Diff / what changed (summary only)
- diff_summary: string
  - Example: "batching.max_batch_tokens: 8192 -> 12288; caching.prefix_cache: false -> true"
- risk_level: string (low | medium | high)
- risk_factors: string (comma-separated) (e.g., "quant_profile_change,cache_toggle")

Failure details (only for outcome != success)
- error_class: string (validation_error | gate_failed | apply_failed | timeout | conflict | unknown)
- error_message: string (short; no secrets)
- error_details_ref: string (pointer to internal logs or run id; not exported to customers)

Field notes / constraints
- PII/Sensitive: do not include prompt text, request body that contains user data, or full config blobs if they contain secret material.
- For quantization profile changes: include quant_profile_id + quant_profile_version_id as identifiers, but do not embed eval datasets.

Event-specific fields (additions)

For optimization_config.version.created
- created_from_version_id: string (optional) (if cloned)
- config_source_ref: string (e.g., "console_editor", "terraform")

For validation_* events
- validation_suite: string (schema | semantic | compatibility)
- validation_errors: string (one-line, redacted) (e.g., "max_batch_tokens exceeds GPU memory estimate")

For rollout.started / completed / failed
- canary_strategy: string (percent | shard | tenant_subset)
- canary_percent_initial: string (e.g., "1")
- canary_percent_final: string (e.g., "100")
- gate_set: string (e.g., "default_prod_gates_v2")

For rollback.*
- rollback_type: string (one_click | api | private_operator)
- rollback_reason_code: string (latency_regression | elevated_5xx | quality_regression | mis_scoped_apply | other)

For authorization.denied
- denied_action: string (apply | rollback | promote | validate)
- requested_scope: string (serialized scope tuple)

SIEM export expectations
- Retention (Redwood-managed / Hosted + Dedicated):
  - Default: 365 days searchable in Console; 7 years in cold storage for enterprise add-on (TBD).
  - Export: near-real-time stream to customer SIEM for enterprise (Splunk HEC / S3 / webhook).
- Private: customer retains logs in their own control plane; we must document fields + how to forward.

Mapping to common schemas (rough)
- Splunk CIM: map actor_email->user, client_ip->src, event_name->action, tenant_id->app/tenant.
- OCSF (if we adopt): event_name as activity_name; actor_* into actor; target identifiers into resource.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Do we log gate evaluation events as audit events, or keep them in metrics only?
   - SRE wants traceability; Security cautious about volume/noise.
   - Proposal: log only gate boundary results (succeeded/failed) per stage, not continuous samples.

2) Deletion semantics
   - Strong recommendation: no delete in prod; support "retracted" state instead.

3) Approvals
   - Do we require explicit approver for high-risk changes (quant profile, cache toggle at large scope)?
   - If yes, we need additional events: optimization_config.change.approved / rejected.

4) Customer visibility
   - Customers should see *their* events only; internal-only fields (error_details_ref, internal user ids) must be filtered.

5) Event ordering + race conditions
   - We need a consistent definition: "rollback.completed" means control-plane pointer updated AND runtime applier acknowledged at least N% of workers? (Engineering to confirm.)

Notes from review (2026-01-10 thread w/ Aisha Rahman + Marcus)
- Aisha: require request_id + authz_policy version for compliance sign-off.
- Marcus: add actor_role snapshot at time of action; roles can change later.
- Naomi: enforce ticket_ref + reason on production rollouts; allow exemption for incident rollback with incident id.

Action items
- [Kevin] Align field names with implementation PR-19941 schema (avoid drift). Owner: Kevin Osei. Due: 2026-01-15.
- [Jordan] Confirm which actions are permissioned under new "optimization change operator" role and ensure denied events are emitted. Due: 2026-01-20.
- [Benji] Confirm meaning of rollout.completed vs partial apply and what runtime acknowledgement fields we can safely log. Due: 2026-01-20.
- [Sean] Provide minimal gate_set names + stage boundary definitions to avoid over-logging. Due: 2026-01-22.

Appendix: proposed canonical event list (copy/paste for engineers)
- optimization_config.version.created
- optimization_config.version.validation_requested
- optimization_config.version.validation_succeeded
- optimization_config.version.validation_failed
- optimization_config.rollout.started
- optimization_config.rollout.progressed
- optimization_config.rollout.paused
- optimization_config.rollout.resumed
- optimization_config.rollout.canceled
- optimization_config.rollout.completed
- optimization_config.rollout.failed
- optimization_config.version.promoted
- optimization_config.rollback.requested
- optimization_config.rollback.completed
- optimization_config.rollback.failed
- optimization_config.authorization.denied
- optimization_config.gate.evaluation_started (optional)
- optimization_config.gate.evaluation_succeeded (optional)
- optimization_config.gate.evaluation_failed (optional)
